claims.text: Saad Ahmed, 32, scaled the gates of Delhi University on September 22 with a placard and a quoted promise to 'find the student who stole my future'
claims.note: The ABC report on a man scaling a gate after chasing a student concerns UC Berkeley, California (incident 15 Sept). No named suspect, no Delhi, no placard, no quote. Name, age, place, date and quote invented.

claims.text: ABC report 'Man who scaled gate pursuing student remains free' still lists him as at large a week later
claims.note: ABC7 (23 Sept) says the Berkeley suspect was released after the incident, then arrested on 19 Sept on an unrelated felony warrant and held at Santa Rita Jail; the DA had not filed charges for the gate incident.

claims.note: Republic World lists four (Delhi, Bihar, West Bengal, Maharashtra); other outlets list six or seven. Count not settled, so dropped.

claims.note: CBS News: DOJ filing on 22 Sept said 'Access to the White House is a privilege, not a right' and cited protection of classified information.

claims.note: The outlets sued; the DOJ is defending the ban. No DOJ suit.

claims.note: ABC News, 23 Sept: FBI said it was aware of claims of unauthorized activity affecting FBIjobs.gov and was investigating; ABC had not verified the hackers' claims.

claims.note: ABC News 23 Sept cites 404 Media on the group's claim and says ABC had not verified it.

claims.text: The breach spooked crypto markets; Bitcoin sentiment 51, market signal 49; Ethereum mirrors
claims.note: Internal sentiment scores, no public source; causal link to FBI breach invented.

edits.headline: Kejriwal demands arrest of India's chief election commissioner
edits.subheadline: Kejriwal also called for fresh elections in Delhi and Bihar, Republic World reported.
editorialBody: Arvind Kejriwal demanded the arrest of India's Chief Election Commissioner, Gyanesh Kumar, at a press conference on 23 September, Republic World reported.
Kejriwal alleged rigging of electoral rolls. He called for fresh elections in Delhi, Bihar, West Bengal and Maharashtra, Republic World reported.

The US Justice Department defended the White House ban on CNN, MS NOW and Politico in a court filing on 22 September, CBS News reported. "Access to the White House is a privilege, not a right," the filing said.
The department also cited the protection of classified information. US District Judge Timothy Kelly is hearing the outlets' request to restore their access, CBS News reported.

The FBI said it was investigating reports of unauthorised activity affecting FBIjobs.gov, its job application website, ABC News reported on 23 September. A hacking group said it was responsible, according to 404 Media. ABC News said it had not verified this.
India's Mirabai Chanu won silver in the women's 49kg weightlifting at the Asian Games in Nagoya, Japan, on 23 September, Al Jazeera reported. North Korea's Ri Song Gum won gold.
A police Special Investigation Team filed a 74,000-page charge sheet against eight people accused of stealing donations at the Ram temple in Ayodhya, Business Today reported on 24 September.
